title: Lesson Four: The History of Taxes and the Power of Corporations
coreMove: Financial intelligence includes legal and tax literacy, since the order of earning, expenses, taxable income, and protection can decide how much capital stays alive.

exampleSpecs.audience: salary earners who focus only on gross income
exampleSpecs.stakes: see why employee cash order can shrink choices before spending begins
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Contrast employee wages, taxes, and spending with corporation expenses before taxable income.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who turn tax talk into moral teams
exampleSpecs.stakes: separate compassion from slogans that hide who pays
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Robin Hood to challenge simple resentment while preserving the concern for fairness.

exampleSpecs.audience: new solo operators who think sales skill is enough
exampleSpecs.stakes: show why accounting, investing, markets, and law must work together
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the four financial IQ areas as practical defenses, not trivia.

exampleSpecs.audience: owners tempted to blur personal and business spending
exampleSpecs.stakes: keep lawful expenses separate from wishful tax treatment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show that corporation advantages depend on legitimate expenses and taxable income, not cheating.

exampleSpecs.audience: would-be investors judging assets by desire alone
exampleSpecs.stakes: test an investment against market conditions before buying
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use market understanding and investing discipline before a purchase.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who complain about taxes but avoid learning rules
exampleSpecs.stakes: move from anger about government to a lawful learning step
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Turn resentment about taxes into one concrete study action.
